title: Retrofit of the Large Integration Hall at the ESO HQ.
description: Division: 06.05.2021. In order to test sensitive instruments in the Large Integration Hall (LIH, size: L 21.5 x W 16.2 x H 13.7m) of the Technical Building (construction from 2014) at ESO premises in Garching the existing HVAC-installations need to be re-designed. Therefore it needs to be checked if existing components need to be retrofitted or complemented or – more likely – a completely new HVAC-system needs to be installed after removing the old equipment. Involved trades are HVAC, electrical works and measurement, control and regulation technology. Ventilation and refrigeration technology have to be changed in a way that pre-defined room conditions can be achieved at all times during the year. (temperature and humidity, air flow, cleanliness aspects have to be considered as well) Additional process cooling for cooling instruments also has to be provided in the same course. Several smaller works such as a new ventilation system in the basement and an exhaust extraction system in a workshop also have to be realized. The project is divided into two parts: 1. the complete planning work, including cost-calculations, a detailed planning and construction management including the support during the complete warranty period 2. the whole construction works, consisting works on HVAC-system, electrical works and management and control system that will remain in place and only has to be complemented. Two possible models regarding the construction works are considered: 2.1. General Contractor including all three trades as well as smaller structural works 2.2. Several single contracts, where HVAC will be the major one. The PI/CFT for the planning work will be released in Q2/2021 to potential suppliers in the ESO Member States and will be followed by a CFT for the construction planned to be issued in Q4/2021. The project will be awarded to Bidders, which have submitted a fully compliant Tender and offer the best value for money for ESO taking into account the quality and price of the offer. description: This tender is for the purchase of a high-volume 3D micro-extrusion printer equipped with continuous paste feeding, vision technology and a plate handling system. The printer distinguishes itself from other 3D printers that are standard on the market due to the combination of a large printing capacity (high volume – max 20 liter paste per hour), a high resolution, a good reproducibility and a high amount of vision systems and data capture. For this, the 3D printer must be custom designed and built. Key conceptual decisions that will be made relate to the extrusion system, the intended production volume, how paste is fed to the extrusion system, how printed materials are removed and how many and which sensors are needed for data capture. title: DEVELOPMENT OF PVA AND BLANKET TECHNOLOGIES FOR SATURN MISSIONS SOLAR ARRAYS - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: ObjectivesTo develop fully European PhotoVoltaic (PVA) and Blanket technologies that can be used on a Solar Array for deep space missions to Saturn.DescriptionLarge solar arrays are currently being developed for telecommunication and scientific missions. Recent examples include the semi-rigid ENEO array, the fully flexible SolarFlex array of the Novacom 2 telecommunications satellite and the rigid array of the JUICE mission to Jupiter. With a high specific power, such arrays lend themselves for use in exploration missions. Feasibility studies have demonstrated that missions to Saturn, fully powered by solar arrays, are indeed feasible. In a recent development activity, the feasibility of a solar array architecture scalable up to 100 m2 per wing and with the capability to retract and re-deploy, to protect the array from damage, has been successfully demonstrated. In the frame of this study, the development of PVA and Blanket frame technologies suitable for the Saturn environment has been indicated as the main focus point for further development of suchsolar array architecture. Saturn environment places demanding requirements on PVA and Blanket technologies: the PVA shall be capable to supply power at very low temperatures and Sun intensities,and the blanket shall be lightweight yet strong enough to support the PVA and to sustain the large temperature range of a Saturn mission. Also, the blanket structure interface shall allow smooth deployment/retraction operations. The activity therefore encompasses the following tasks: Investigation into actual PVA LILT technologies and potential adaptations for its use on a Saturn mission (e.g. reduced thickness) Definition of blanket and blanket frame design, to act as PVA support and able to cope with the required temperature range Demonstration via mechanical and electrical analyses of the suitability of the selected design for the Saturn mission Demonstration of the suitability of the selectedtechnologies for the Saturn mission by means of thermal cycling and vibration tests of a representative Blanket segment (PVA and blanket) mock-up Identification of development needs Preparation of a roadmap
